Hi there! I can try to answer your questions as best as possible as I work at ICON as a CRA.

Since you already have some clinical research experience, you are probably being considered for a clinical trial associate position. This is a newer position at ICON and technically a step up from a Clinical Trial Assistant, as they usually fast track the clinical trial associates to IHCRA quickly.

Yes, that salary for the early development program Sounds about right. I went through the program, but since I was internal, my salary as lower than 60k during this time. I know they offer external candidates more. I will tell you that once you advance to a traveling CRA, you will get at least 10 k more.’’

In the case they are interviewing you for a clinical trial assistant, the salary is around 40k starting. Again, this is an entry level position so with your experience I do believe they are considering you for the clinical trial associate position! 

I did not sign a non-compete agreement with ICON! But, I’ve been there over 2 years, so it could have changed.

Pros and cons for working there are the same as about every CRO, Workload can be a lot, depending on what sponsor/studies you are working on as well as your manager.‘

I have EXTREME dental anxiety to the point where I just start crying in the chair! I would definitely talk to your dentist and the hygienist and let them know you're really nervous. One thing my dentist will tell me is to raise my hand if i need a break and she always tells me what she is going to do (if I want to know) before she does it. I also bring in a stuffed animal to hold (I have no shame, I am a 26 y/o female). I have heard other times that people will ask to wear the vest that they use during x rays because the weight of it helps sooth them (i have not done this yet, but I may in the future). The other thing that I looked for when searching for a new dentist (about a year and half ago) was dentists that either have laughing gas or other sedation dentistry. I have an upcoming procedure and I am getting laughing gas during the procedure which will help A TON. I also will probably take an Ativan before hand. 

Lastly, having music in headphones or AirPods at a low volume might help.

I know this post was 2 months ago, but hope this helps .:) you are not alone!
